haiku-low.q1: They see "If an account exists for that address, we've sent a link." Nothing is sent.
haiku-low.q2: The request gets the same generic message, but no token is created and no email is sent. The limit is 3 rows per account in the last hour.
haiku-low.q3: 30 minutes, and it works once. It ends sooner if it is used, or if a newer link is issued for the same account.
haiku-low.q4: It stays valid: unused and not dead. The user can retry until it expires.
haiku-low.q5: None. All sessions for the account are deleted, including the resetter's. The user is sent to the login page and must log in again with the new password.
haiku-low.q6: The worker retries 3 times with backoff, then logs the failure and drops the job. The user is not told.
haiku-low.q7: The raw token is put into the email job's link when the job is added to the Email queue. The worker then sends it; only the hash is stored.
haiku-low.q8: It hashes the link's token with SHA-256 and finds the matching reset_tokens row. It is valid if found, under 30 minutes old, unused and not dead.
haiku-low.q9: No separate counter; it counts reset_tokens rows for the account created in the last hour, of every state. Old rows drop out as they pass one hour.
haiku-low.q10: Its earlier unused tokens are marked dead in the same transaction as the new token's insert, before the email job is queued.
haiku-low.q11: In one transaction: mark the token used, save the new password hash, and delete all the account's sessions. The confirmation email is queued after the commit.
haiku-low.q12: The update marks the token used only if it is still unused. One submit wins; the other changes no row, rolls back, and sees the expired page.

sonnet.q1: They see the generic message "If an account exists for that address, we've sent a link." Nothing is sent.
sonnet.q2: The rate limit (3 per account per rolling hour) is hit: no token is created and nothing is sent, but the user still sees the same generic message.
sonnet.q3: 30 minutes. It ends sooner if used (password saved), or if a newer link is issued for the same account (the earlier unused token becomes dead).
sonnet.q4: Still valid and unused. The reason is shown and the user can retry until it expires (30 minutes).
sonnet.q5: None; all sessions rows for the account are deleted, including the resetting person's. They are redirected to the login page (no automatic login) and log in with the new password.
sonnet.q6: The worker retries up to 3 times with backoff, then logs the failure and drops the job. The user is not notified; they must request another link (which counts toward the limit).
sonnet.q7: The raw token (32 random bytes) is generated at request time, its hash is stored, and after the commit the raw token is put in the link in the email job added to the Email queue; the worker sends it.
sonnet.q8: It hashes the token from the link and looks it up in reset_tokens. Valid if found, under 30 minutes old, unused and not dead; otherwise it shows the expired page. Opening changes nothing in the database.
sonnet.q9: No separate counter. It is computed by counting reset_tokens rows (all states) for the account created in the last hour; old rows drop out as they age past one hour (rolling window).
sonnet.q10: The account's earlier unused tokens are marked dead, in the same transaction as inserting the new token row (before the commit and email job).
sonnet.q11: In one transaction: the token is marked used, the new password hash is saved in users, and all the account's sessions rows are deleted. The "password was changed" email job is queued after the commit.
sonnet.q12: The update that marks the token used only applies if it is still unused. One submit changes a row and wins; the other changes no row, rolls back and sees the expired page.
